title: Encrypted DNS Provisioning RFC 9464 Response Policy Architecture
purpose: Define the RFC 9464 encrypted DNS provisioning request/reply policy boundary above the ENCDNS_IP* and ENCDNS_DIGEST_INFO byte codecs.
design_summary: The response-policy slice adds pure helpers for constructing CFG_REQUEST support advertisements, deduplicating identical request attributes, optionally discarding overly repetitive requests, selecting supported CFG_REPLY ENCDNS_IP* configurations by requested address family, ignoring suggested resolver values when responder policy supplies its own configuration, returning multiple matching configurations ordered by service priority, and optionally attaching CFG_REPLY ENCDNS_DIGEST_INFO. The policy consumes the existing validated attribute and digest codecs rather than owning IKEv2 session state.
data_and_state_considerations: The helpers are deterministic value selectors. They do not parse complete IKEv2 messages, negotiate IPsec, provision operating-system resolver state, open encrypted DNS sessions, or validate certificates.
edge_cases_and_constraints: A support advertisement must include ENCDNS_IP4, ENCDNS_IP6, or both.
Only CFG_REQUEST attributes are accepted as responder input.
Available configurations must be CFG_REPLY ENCDNS_IP* attributes with at least one IP address.
Identical duplicate request attributes are ignored until the configured threshold permits discarding the request.
Returned configurations are sorted by service priority, where lower values are preferred.
risks: This slice does not implement RFC 7296 notify/error payloads for malformed attributes.
This slice does not implement full IKEv2 exchange integration or resolver-install policy.
This slice does not perform certificate-chain validation; digest information remains caller-provided.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The policy is intentionally above the RFC 9464 byte codec and below any future IKEv2 integration. It lets ProtocolLab or higher-level provisioning code select response values without coupling the QUIC transport runtime to IPsec configuration exchange behavior.
